name: canli-markets-mcp

tools.name: enforcement_actions
tools.description: The SEC's latest enforcement: litigation releases and administrative proceedings, with who was named, the number and the document, across the market or filtered to a company or person (every word of the name must match). The feeds hold the latest actions only, so an empty answer is limited to what they reach.

company.description: A company or person, every word of it in the case's name. Leave out for all the latest actions.

limit.description: Most actions; default 25.

tools.name: consumer_complaints
tools.description: Complaints consumers sent the CFPB about a bank, lender, card issuer or credit bureau: totals, the last 12 months, top products and issues, and how often the company answered in time. Complaints are unverified and not adjusted for size.

company.description: Ticker or name, as the bank or lender is known: "Wells Fargo", "JPM", "Experian".

tools.name: product_recalls
tools.description: Recalls: a firm's FDA recalls of drugs, devices and food with class, reason and status, and a vehicle's NHTSA safety recalls by make, model and year.

company.description: Ticker or name of the recalling firm: its FDA recalls of drugs, devices and food.

vehicle.description: A vehicle's NHTSA safety recalls, e.g. {make: "ford", model: "f-150", year: 2023}.

limit.description: Most recalls of each kind, newest first; default 10.

tools.name: sanctions_check
tools.description: Search the U.S. Treasury's Specially Designated Nationals list and its aliases for a person, company, bank or vessel, by whole words. Not a compliance screening: no match is not clearance, and a match needs checking against the entry.

name.description: A person, company, bank or vessel. Every word must be in the listed name or an alias, in any order.

limit.description: Most listings; default 20.

tools.name: federal_rules
tools.description: Federal Register documents: final and proposed rules, notices and presidential documents by words and agency (SEC, CFTC, Fed, Treasury, CFPB, FDA and more), with comment deadlines, effective dates and abstracts. Can list only rules still open for comment.

query.description: Words to find, e.g. "climate disclosure" or "stablecoin".

agency.description: One of: sec, cftc, fed, treasury, occ, cfpb, fdic, irs, ftc, fcc, epa, fda, faa, doe, ferc, bis, ofac, hhs.

type.description: Final rules, proposed rules, notices or presidential documents; default all.

since.description: Published on or after this date.

open_for_comment.description: Only those whose comment period has not closed.

limit.description: Most documents, newest first; default 15.

tools.name: technical_indicators
tools.description: The common technical indicators for a symbol in one call, from its daily prices: moving averages (SMA and EMA), RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands and ATR, with where the close sits against its 50- and 200-day averages. Standard definitions; describes past prices, not a forecast.

as_of.description: Compute as of this date; default the latest close.

tools.name: stock_snapshot
tools.description: What a quote page shows and no primary source publishes, from Yahoo Finance: analysts' mean, median, high and low price targets, how many analysts, the recommendation and ratings, EPS and revenue estimates by quarter and year, market cap, trailing and forward P/E and other ratios, 52-week range, dividend rate, short interest, institutional and insider percentages, next earnings date. Vendor aggregates, labeled as such; for reported figures use the filings.

symbol.description: The ticker on Yahoo Finance: AAPL, BRK-B, 7203.T, SHEL.L.

annotations.title: Analyst targets, valuation and short interest

tools.name: security_identifiers
tools.description: Map a ticker, ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL or FIGI to one security through OpenFIGI: its name, FIGIs, listings, exchange and type. Check digits are tested first, so a mistyped ISIN or CUSIP is refused.

id.description: A ticker, ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL or FIGI; the kind is read from its form.

exchange.description: OpenFIGI's exchange code, for a ticker: US (default), LN, GR, JP, HK...

limit.description: Most listings; default 20.

tools.name: legal_entity
tools.description: Who a company legally is, from the Global LEI register: legal name, LEI, jurisdiction, status, addresses, former names, its direct and ultimate parents and how many entities it owns. By name or LEI; works for firms worldwide, listed or not.

name.description: A legal name, e.g. "Apple Inc." or "Deutsche Bank". Every word must be in the name.

limit.description: Other entities of that name to list; default 5.

tools.name: world_yields
tools.description: Government bond yields side by side: U.S. Treasury, euro area (ECB, AAA), UK (Bank of England), Japan (Ministry of Finance) and Canada (Bank of Canada), by maturity, with the date and basis of each curve, 10Y-2Y slopes and 10-year spreads to the U.S.

tools.name: credit_cycle
tools.description: The BIS credit cycle by country: private credit as a share of GDP, its long-run trend and the credit-to-GDP gap, an early-warning measure regulators use for banking stress. Up to 40 quarters.

quarters.description: Quarters of history for each; default 8.

tools.name: dividend_history
tools.description: A security's dividends and splits: each payment by ex-date, totals by year, the trailing 12-month yield, five-year growth and the streak of rising annual totals. Works for foreign listings.

symbol.description: Ticker, e.g. KO, or a foreign listing such as NESN.SW.

tools.name: verify_claims
tools.description: Check a draft answer's figures against the company's own filings before using them: revenue, net income, EPS, operating income, margins, growth, cash flow, assets, debt and more, for a fiscal year or quarter as the company labels it. US and foreign filers (20-F, IFRS), in their own currency. Each claim comes back confirmed, contradicted (with the filed figure and what the claimed one matches instead: another year, a quarter, a unit slip), not reported or not checkable.

company.description: Ticker (AAPL, NVO, TSM), CIK (320193) or name: the company the claims are about. Foreign companies filing 20-F or 40-F are checked too, in the currency they report in.

claims.description: Claims to check, each a measure, period and value.

measure.description: What the figure is: revenue, net income, diluted EPS, operating income, gross profit, operating margin, net margin, free cash flow, total assets, cash, long-term debt, R&D, dividends per share...

period.description: The period as the company labels it: "fiscal 2025", "FY2025", "2025", "Q3 2026", "third quarter of fiscal 2026", or a span by its end date: "three months ended June 28, 2025".

value.description: The claimed figure, as written: 416.2 with unit "USD billion"; margins and growth in percent.

unit.description: "USD billion", "EUR million", "DKK billion", "USD per share", "%". A currency the company does not report in is a conversion and is not judged.

growth.description: The value is growth over the prior year, in percent.

basis.description: Adjusted and non-GAAP figures are not in the XBRL statements and are not checked here.

text.description: Or a draft answer about the company: every figure in it with a measure and a period is checked.

tools.name: exposure_map
tools.description: Who depends on a company, from what others say in their annual reports: every filer that names it, with the passage, and whether it reads as a supplier, customer or competitor. For supply chains no fund report shows. Read by rules, so check the passage.

name.description: The company or thing to follow, as filings write it, such as Taiwan Semiconductor.

also.description: Other names for it, such as TSMC.

since.description: Filed since this date; default about 15 months ago, so each filer's latest annual report is in.

limit.description: Most filers to read; default 20, and 10 on the hosted server.

tools.name: guidance_record
tools.description: A management team's record against its own word: each quarter it gave guidance in its press release, what it said and what then happened, how often results came in above, within and below its own range, and which quarters fell short.

quarters.description: How many results releases to go back through; default 12.

measure.description: Only this measure, such as revenue or eps.

filed_before.description: Start from the latest release filed by this date.

annotations.title: Management's record against its own guidance

tools.name: what_happened_next
tools.description: Every past time a market or stock fell, rose or sat this far below its high: each case, what followed a month, a quarter and a year later, the worst and best, and how that compares with an ordinary day. A record, not a forecast or advice.

symbol.description: A market or ticker: S&P 500 (default), Nasdaq, AAPL, BTC-USD.

condition.description: fell or rose: by percent within days. below_high: at least percent under its highest close so far. new_high: a new highest close.

percent.description: How far; needed for all but new_high.

days.description: For fell and rose: within this many trading days; default 21, about a month.

horizons.description: Trading days ahead to look; default 21, 63, 126 and 252 (a month, a quarter, six months, a year).

since.description: First date to look from; default as far back as the prices go.

gap_days.description: Episodes must be at least this many trading days apart, so one slide is not counted many times; default 63.

annotations.title: What happened next, every past time

tools.name: filing_memory
tools.description: Everything one company has said about a subject across every annual report it has on EDGAR, back to the 1990s where they exist: the best passages with links, how often it came up each year, and optionally how that moved with a margin, tested against chance. Reads the reports on this machine; no key. Supply the company's likely words in also and all_of, since a company rarely uses yours.

query.description: The subject in plain words, for example "supply chain problems in Southeast Asia". Quote a phrase to keep its words together.

also.description: Other words a company might use for the same subject, which you supply, such as contract manufacturer, Vietnam, Thailand. They help the ranking.

all_of.description: What counts as a mention: a paragraph must hold at least one term from every group, such as [["supply chain","supplier"],["Southeast Asia","Vietnam","Thailand"]]. Without it, a paragraph counts if it holds most of the query's words.

years.description: How many annual reports back; default 20. The hosted server reads at most 10.

section.description: Only one part of each report: "risk factors", "md&a", "business" or an item number such as 1A.

limit.description: Passages to return; default 8.

per_year.description: Most passages from one report; default 2.

filed_before.description: Only reports filed by this date.

correlate_with.description: Compare how often the subject comes up with this measure, year by year, from the company's XBRL (2009 on).

semantic.description: Also rank by meaning with a local embedding model, if one is installed (canli-mcp models install). Helps when a company's words differ from yours and you have supplied no others. The first run over a company's reports takes minutes; later ones are quick.

annotations.title: Search all of a company's annual reports

tools.name: filing_sentiment
tools.description: The tone of a filing or any text, sentence by sentence, from FinBERT run on this machine: an 8-K's press release by default, or a 10-K section. Needs the optional local models (canli-mcp models install). Tone, not truth, and no evidence it predicts a price; the model is licensed for non-commercial use.

text.description: Text to read. Or name a filing with company.

company.description: Read this company's latest filing of form.

form.description: Default 8-K, whose press release (EX-99.1) is read when it has one.

document.description: A document in the filing, such as EX-99.1.

section.description: For a 10-K or 10-Q: a section such as md&a.

tools.name: shipping_activity
tools.description: Ships moving through the world's straits and canals (Suez, Panama, Malacca, Hormuz and others) and ports, from the IMF's PortWatch, which estimates them from satellite tracking of ships. All chokepoints against a year ago, one chokepoint by week, or one port. No key.

chokepoint.description: A strait or canal, such as Suez Canal, Panama Canal, Malacca Strait or Strait of Hormuz. Without chokepoint or port you get every chokepoint.

port.description: A port by name, such as Shanghai or Rotterdam.

start.description: First day; default about 100 days before the last.

end.description: Last day; default today, and the data runs a week or more behind.

tools.name: page_attention
tools.description: Daily Wikipedia page views for a company or subject: a plain measure of public attention, with how the last week compares with normal. No key.

topic.description: A company or subject, such as Nvidia or Bitcoin. The closest English Wikipedia article is used, and its title comes back so you can check it.

days.description: How far back, in days; default 90.

tools.name: latest_price
tools.description: The latest price of a stock, ETF, index, currency or crypto pair, with the previous close and the time of the price. No key; can run late, by 15 minutes or more on some markets.

symbol.description: A ticker (AAPL, BRK.B), a stock listed abroad with its market suffix (SAP.DE, 7203.T, SHEL.L, 0700.HK), a currency pair (EUR/USD), a future (CL=F, or "crude oil", "gold"), an index (^GSPC, or "S&P 500", "VIX", "10 year yield") or a crypto pair (BTC/USD, or "bitcoin").

tools.name: european_filings
tools.description: A European company's annual financial report as it filed it in the European Single Electronic Format (ESEF): revenue, operating and net profit, EPS, assets, equity, cash, cash flows and dividends as the company tagged them (IFRS concepts, its currency, full scale), with the comparatives, the report's viewer link and the other years on file. Issuers on EU and EEA regulated markets, found by name or LEI; words find any other tagged figure.

company.description: Company name (ASML, LVMH, TotalEnergies) or its LEI (724500Y6DUVHQD6OXN27).

year.description: Fiscal year the report covers (the year its period ends); default the latest filed.

words.description: Also find the report's other figures whose concept names hold these words ("net system sales", "lease liabilities").

tools.name: reference_rates
tools.description: Money-market and policy rates and the ECB's euro exchange reference rates (fx:GBP) from the central banks themselves: SOFR, TGCR, BGCR, EFFR and OBFR from the New York Fed (with percentiles and volume), the euro short-term rate and the ECB's policy rates, SONIA and Bank Rate from the Bank of England, and about forty central banks' policy rates as the BIS collects them (policy:JP, policy:Brazil). Dates and rates, oldest first.

rate.description: fx:GBP (the ECB's euro reference rate: units of that currency per euro); sofr, tgcr, bgcr, effr or obfr (New York Fed); estr, ecb_deposit, ecb_refi or ecb_marginal (ECB); sonia or bank_rate (Bank of England); or policy:<country>, a central bank's policy rate as the BIS collects it (policy:JP, policy:Brazil, policy:euro area).

start.description: First date; default 90 days before end.

tools.name: prediction_markets
tools.description: What traders on Polymarket and Kalshi are paying for an outcome, found by words (a Fed decision, a recession, an election, a price level): each market's probability (the middle of bid and ask, else the last trade), bid, ask, volume and closing date, with the event's resolution rules.

query.description: What the market is about, in words: "fed rate cut", "recession 2026", "bitcoin 150k".

limit.description: Most events per venue; default 6.

tools.name: crypto_fundamentals
tools.description: A DeFi protocol's total value locked (now, by chain, and its history), the fees users pay it and the revenue it keeps (24 hours to all time); a chain's total value locked; or a stablecoin's supply in circulation and its change, by chain. From DefiLlama's open data.

protocol.description: A DeFi protocol by name or DefiLlama slug: aave, lido, uniswap, maker, pendle.

chain.description: A chain's total value locked: Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum, Base.

stablecoin.description: A stablecoin's supply in circulation: USDT, USDC, DAI, USDe.

days.description: Days of history to return; default 365.

tools.name: financial_statements
tools.description: A company's financial statements exactly as filed: income statement, balance sheet, cash flow and equity statement from its 10-K (or 10-Q), with its own line labels, each line's XBRL concept and the values as the filing shows them (units say the scale). Joins several filings by period; a line a later filing restated, or that a stock split changed, is shown beside its first-reported figure, never mixed in.

statement.description: Which statement: income, balance_sheet, cash_flow, comprehensive_income, equity; core (default) is the first three, all is every one.

period.description: annual (10-K, default) or quarterly (10-Q: each quarter and the year to date; the fourth quarter is only in the 10-K's year).

filings.description: How many 10-Ks (or 10-Qs) to read and join by period, newest first; default 1. One 10-K holds three years of income and cash flows and two balance sheets, so 2 covers four years and 3 covers five.

fiscal_year.description: Start from the 10-K for the fiscal year ending in this calendar year (or the latest 10-Q of it).

filed_before.description: Start from the latest filing on or before this date: what was known then.

tools.name: filing_tables
tools.description: The table in a filing that holds a figure, found by words ("paid members", "revenue by region", "guidance"): XBRL statement and detail reports and the tables in the document itself (MD&A figures such as members, stores or ARPU), or an 8-K press release's tables. With filings above one, the same words in each earlier filing, to follow a figure over the years. Without words, lists the tables.

find.description: Words the table holds, in its title or its row labels: "paid members", "revenue by region", "share repurchases", "adjusted EPS reconciliation"; quote a phrase. Without find, the filing's tables are listed.

form.description: 10-K (default), 10-Q, 8-K (a results press release's tables), DEF 14A (proxy), 20-F, S-1...

filings.description: Look in this many filings of the form, newest first, to follow a figure over the years; default 1. Needs find.

filed_before.description: Start from the latest filing of the form on or before this date.

document.description: Search this document of the filing instead (by type or file name, "EX-99.2"); default the main document, or an 8-K's press release.

max_tables.description: Most tables shown per filing; default 3.

tools.name: earnings_release
tools.description: A quarter's results press release (8-K Item 2.02): the headline, the results it states (each with the part of the business it belongs to and what a change is measured against), its guidance parsed into ranges (low, high, midpoint, unit, measure, basis, period, and the sentence or table row), and the previous release's guidance for this quarter set against the company's results: above, within or below the range, in basis points for rates.

accession.description: A results 8-K; default the latest (earnings_calendar lists them).

filed_before.description: The latest results release filed on or before this date.

compare.description: Line up the previous release's guidance for this quarter against these results; default true.

tools.name: release_check
tools.description: A quarter's results press release set against the 10-Q or 10-K filed after it: every figure in the release's tables looked for among the report's inline XBRL facts for the same period. Lists the figures that changed (release value, filed value, difference, percent, the XBRL concept and how the line was matched), release figures with no counterpart (non-GAAP measures, metrics) and lines the report adds, such as a charge booked after the release.

period.description: The quarter: its end date (2026-06-30; a few days off is fine for 52-53 week years) or a fiscal label (Q2 2026, FY2025: the fiscal year that ends in that year). Default: the latest quarter whose 10-Q or 10-K is filed.

max_rows.description: Most changed figures and release-only labels listed; default 40.

tools.name: audit_signals
tools.description: What auditors and companies say when something is wrong, from SEC filings. Going-concern doubt: each 10-K and 10-Q whose text says there is substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue, as a timeline (first raised, still raised, lifted), or across the market the companies whose latest report newly raised it. Auditor changes (8-K Item 4.01): who left and who came, resigned or dismissed, disagreements and reportable events. The latest 10-K's critical audit matters. Each row quotes the filing.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name. Without it, across the market: the companies whose latest 10-K or 10-Q newly raised a going-concern doubt, or the auditor changes filed, in the last `days`.

signal.description: going_concern, auditor_change (8-K Item 4.01), critical_audit_matters (the latest 10-K's auditor's report; a company only) or all. Default: all for a company, going_concern across the market.

days.description: Across the market, how many days back from today; default 30.

limit.description: Most rows in each table; default 12 for a company (its latest reports), 10 across the market.

annotations.title: Going-concern doubts, auditor changes and critical audit matters

tools.name: screen_companies
tools.description: Screen every US-listed company (thousands, from SEC XBRL frames) on fundamentals: revenue, growth, margins, ROE, ROA, free cash flow, R&D intensity, leverage and more, for a calendar year or each company's fiscal year ending in a date window, with filters, ranking and optional valuation (price, market cap, P/E, P/S, FCF yield). Implausible figures (tagging slips) are held out and listed apart.

period.description: FY2025 (each company's fiscal year that best overlaps calendar 2025; default the last complete year) or a quarter such as CY2026Q2.

fiscal_year_end.description: Instead of period: each company's fiscal year ending between these dates, e.g. ["2025-02-01", "2026-01-31"]; balance-sheet figures at that year's end.

value.description: A number, or [low, high] for between. Ratios and growth are fractions (0.2 = 20%); money in US dollars.

sort_by.description: Metric to rank by; default the first filter's metric, else revenue.

exchanges.description: Listing venues to include; default NYSE and Nasdaq. "all" includes unlisted filers.

limit.description: Most companies to return; default 25.

valuation.description: Add price, market cap, P/E, P/S and FCF yield for the returned companies (latest close; up to 50 companies).

include_suspect.description: Keep companies whose figures fail a plausibility check (for example net income above 10 times revenue, usually a tagging slip); default false: they are listed apart.

tools.name: company_report
tools.description: One company in one call: profile, five fiscal years of financials (revenue, growth, margins, net income, EPS, cash flow, ROE, leverage), price and risk over a year (return, volatility, drawdown, beta), valuation (market cap, P/E, P/S, FCF yield), insider buying and selling, and recent filings, each from its source.

tools.name: event_study
tools.description: How a stock's price reacted to events: earnings releases (8-K item 2.02), insider purchases or sales (Form 4), any 8-K, or given dates. Abnormal returns against a market model, cumulative abnormal return per event and on average, with a t test across events. For filings use event_type (with last for the most recent few), not filing dates: it starts day 0 at the first session after the SEC accepted the filing.

events.description: Event dates: day 0 is that date, or the next trading day if markets were shut. For filings use event_type instead: a filing made after the close moves the price the next session, and only event_type times that.

event_type.description: Events from SEC filings: earnings (8-K item 2.02), open-market insider purchases or sales (Form 4 codes P or S, at filing time), or any 8-K. Day 0 is the first trading session after the filing was accepted.

since.description: For event_type: filings since this date; default three years ago.

last.description: For event_type: only the most recent this many events, such as 8 for the last 8 earnings releases.

window.description: Event window in trading days around day 0; default [-1, 5].

estimation_days.description: Days used to fit the model, ending 10 days before the window; default 120.

benchmark.description: Market index for the model; default SPY.

model.description: market (OLS alpha and beta on the benchmark, default), market_adjusted (return minus benchmark) or mean_adjusted.

tools.name: mentions_trend
tools.description: How often a word or phrase appears in SEC filings over time (by month, quarter or year), across all filers or one company, from EDGAR full-text search: for themes such as "tariffs", "agentic AI" or "going concern".

query.description: Words or a quoted phrase, for example "\"artificial intelligence\"" or tariffs.

start.description: First day; default three years ago.

tools.name: company_profile
tools.description: A company's or fund's SEC profile by ticker, CIK or name: tickers, exchange, industry (SIC), fiscal year end, state, address, former names, and its latest 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K and 13F.

tools.name: list_filings
tools.description: A company's SEC filings, newest first, filtered by form type (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEF 14A, S-1, 4, 13F-HR...) and dates, with links. Use read_filing to read one.

forms.description: Form types, for example ["10-K", "8-K"]; amendments (10-K/A) are included. Default: all.

form.description: One form type, the same as forms with one entry.

since.description: Filed on or after this date.

until.description: Filed on or before this date.

limit.description: Most filings, newest first; default 20.

tools.name: read_filing
tools.description: The text of an SEC filing: the latest of a form, or one by accession. For a 10-K or 10-Q, section returns one item ("risk factors", "md&a", "business", "market risk", "legal proceedings", or a number such as "1A"); without it the result lists the items and their lengths. document reads an exhibit, such as an 8-K's press release ("EX-99.1"). find returns only the passages with given words ("employees", "buyback"), the fastest way to a fact in a long filing; otherwise long text pages with offset.

accession.description: The filing; from list_filings or search_filings.

form.description: Without accession: read the company's latest filing of this form; default 10-K.

filed_before.description: Without accession: the latest filing of the form filed on or before this date.

section.description: 10-K or 10-Q item: "risk factors", "md&a", "business", "market risk", "legal proceedings", "1A", "7"; the result lists every item found.

document.description: Another document in the filing, by file name or type, for example "EX-99.1" (an 8-K's press release).

find.description: Words to find in the filing (or section), for example "employees" or "share repurchase": returns the matching passages with their offsets instead of the text from the start. Quote a phrase to match it exactly.

offset.description: Character offset to continue from; the previous result's next_offset, or a find match's offset.

tools.name: search_filings
tools.description: Full-text search across all SEC filings since 2001 (EDGAR full-text search): which companies mention a phrase, filtered by form, filer and dates. Quote phrases.

query.description: Words to find in filing text; put a phrase in double quotes, for example "\"supply chain\" tariffs".

forms.description: Form types, for example ["10-K"]. Default: all.

limit.description: Most documents; default 10.

tools.name: insider_trades
tools.description: Insider transactions at a company from its Form 4 filings: who (officers, directors, 10% owners), what (open-market buys and sales, option exercises, tax withholding, gifts), shares, price, value, holdings after, and 10b5-1 plan flags, with a buy/sell summary. Default: the last 90 days.

since.description: Filed on or after; default 90 days ago.

until.description: Filed on or before; default today.

codes.description: Transaction codes to keep, for example ["P", "S"] for open-market purchases and sales. Default: all.

max_filings.description: Most Form 4 filings to read, newest first; default 40.

tools.name: fund_holdings
tools.description: A fund manager's 13F holdings for a quarter (latest by default): positions by value with portfolio weights, the total checked against the filing's cover page, and what changed since the previous quarter (new, exited, added, reduced).

manager.description: The 13F filer: name ("Berkshire Hathaway", "Bridgewater Associates"), ticker or CIK.

period.description: Quarter end, for example 2026-06-30; default the latest filed.

top.description: Most positions to list, by value; default 25.

compare.description: Also compare with the previous quarter's filing; default true.

tools.name: unusual_options
tools.description: Unusual options activity for a stock, ETF or index from Cboe's delayed quotes: contracts trading at least as many times their open interest as asked (new positions more likely than closing), ranked by the premium that changed hands, with strike, expiry, IV and delta, and the day's call and put premium.

symbol.description: A stock or ETF (AAPL, SPY) or an index (SPX, NDX).

min_volume.description: Only contracts with at least this many traded today; default 100.

min_ratio.description: Volume at least this many times the open interest; default 1.

limit.description: Most contracts, largest premium first; default 20.

tools.name: company_emissions
tools.description: A company's greenhouse-gas emissions from its US facilities as they reported them to EPA (the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program): direct emissions in tonnes of CO2e, the company's ownership share of them, by gas, the largest facilities, and a trend over up to five years. Scope 1 from the measurements, not a vendor's ESG score.

company.description: The parent company as its facilities name it: "Exxon", "Duke Energy", "Dow".

year.description: The reporting year; default the latest EPA has published (data for a year comes out the autumn after).

trend.description: Also the total for this many years before, to the year asked for.

top.description: How many facilities to list, largest first; default 10.

tools.name: crypto_markets
tools.description: The crypto market from CoinGecko: coins ranked by market value with price, volume, change over a day, a week and a month, supply and distance from the all-time high, and the whole market's value with bitcoin's and ether's shares; or the coins named, by symbol or CoinGecko id.

coins.description: Coins by symbol (btc, eth) or CoinGecko id (bitcoin, ethereum); default the largest by market value.

limit.description: How many of the largest; default 25.

tools.name: etf_profile
tools.description: What an ETF or mutual fund costs and holds, from Yahoo Finance's fund profile: the expense ratio beside its category's average, turnover, total assets, yield, year-to-date and five-year returns, beta, inception, top holdings with weights, the mix of stocks, bonds and cash, and sector weights.

symbol.description: The fund's ticker on Yahoo Finance: SPY, QQQ, VTI, VFIAX.

annotations.title: ETF or fund profile: costs and holdings

tools.name: market_calendar
tools.description: The whole market's schedule from Nasdaq's public calendars: who reports earnings on given days (before the open or after the close, consensus EPS and number of estimates, last year's EPS), who goes ex-dividend (amount, record and payment dates), stock splits coming up, and a month's IPOs (priced, expected, filed, withdrawn); filter by tickers or market value.

kind.description: earnings: who reports and the consensus EPS; dividends: who goes ex-dividend; splits: splits coming up; ipos: the month's IPOs, priced, expected, filed and withdrawn.

days.description: How many days from date (earnings and dividends); default 1.

min_market_cap.description: Earnings: only companies worth at least this many US dollars.

limit.description: Most rows; default 100, largest companies first for earnings.

tools.name: congress_trades
tools.description: Stock and bond trades by members of the House, read from their periodic transaction reports on the Clerk's site: owner (self, spouse, joint, child), asset and ticker, purchase or sale, trade date, date notified and the amount range, for one member, a state or district, a ticker, or the newest reports filed, with each report's link.

member.description: Part of a member's name: "Pelosi", "Kevin Hern".

district.description: A state's members ("TX") or one district ("CA11").

ticker.description: Only trades in this ticker, among the reports read.

year.description: The year the reports were filed; default this year.

reports.description: How many reports to read, newest first; default 10.

tools.name: analyst_history
tools.description: A stock's analyst history from Yahoo Finance: every upgrade, downgrade, initiation and target change by firm over any window, the last four quarters' earnings surprises, how the EPS estimate moved over 90 days with the analysts revising it up and down, and the rating counts month by month. stock_snapshot has today's targets and estimates. A vendor's aggregates, labeled so.

symbol.description: The ticker on Yahoo Finance: AAPL, BRK-B, 7203.T.

days.description: Rating changes over this many days; default 180.

firm.description: Only this firm's rating changes (part of its name).

annotations.title: Analyst rating changes, surprises and revisions

tools.name: market_movers
tools.description: Today's biggest US stock gainers, losers and most traded (price, change, volume, average volume, market value), or Yahoo Finance's other ready-made lists: small-cap gainers, most shorted, undervalued growth, growth technology, aggressive small caps, undervalued large caps.

list.description: gainers, losers or most_active today (default gainers), or one of Yahoo's ready-made screens: small_cap_gainers, most_shorted, undervalued_growth, growth_technology, aggressive_small_caps, undervalued_large_caps.

tools.name: market_hours
tools.description: The US stock market's calendar (NYSE and Nasdaq): open, pre-market, after-hours or closed now, the next open and close in Eastern time and UTC, a year's holidays and 1 p.m. early closes, whether a date trades, and how many trading days lie between two dates. Computed from NYSE's rules and its unscheduled closures since 2000, with no network.

date.description: A day to ask about: whether it trades, and its hours.

year.description: A year's holidays and early closes.

start.description: With end: how many trading days from start to end, both included.

tools.name: factor_returns
tools.description: The Fama-French factors from Kenneth French's data library at Dartmouth: the market over the T-bill (Mkt-RF), size (SMB), value (HML), profitability (RMW), investment (CMA) and momentum (Mom), with the one-month T-bill rate (RF), monthly since 1926, daily or by year, as fractions ready for a factor regression.

model.description: ff3 (market, size, value), ff5 (adds profitability and investment), momentum, carhart (ff3 and momentum) or ff5_momentum. Default ff3.

start.description: First period: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Default ten years before the latest (one year for daily; every year for annual).

end.description: Last period. Default the latest published.

tools.name: scenario_risk
tools.description: A portfolio's holdings under a macro shock or a past crisis. Shock some of eight factors (US stocks, the 2- and 10-year Treasury yields, the Baa-Aaa spread, oil, the dollar, gold, the VIX) and the rest move as history says they do alongside, with a 90% range; or replay a crisis (2008, 2020, 2022 and eight more) beside each holding's actual return then, with the model's error. Betas from weekly returns over the last years. Local server (prices).

symbol.description: A stock, ETF or fund as price_history reads it (AAPL, TLT, SAP.DE).

weight.description: Its share of the portfolio's value as a fraction (0.25 is a quarter; negative for a short).

holdings.description: The portfolio, up to 25 holdings. Weights are used as given: they need not sum to 1 (a hedged book can sum to 0).

shocks.description: A hypothetical scenario: the factors you move. Those you leave out move by what history implies given yours.

equities.description: US stocks' return, as a fraction (-0.2 is a 20% fall).

rates_2y.description: The 2-year Treasury yield's change in percentage points (0.5 is 50 basis points).

rates_10y.description: The 10-year Treasury yield's change in percentage points.

credit_spread.description: The Baa-over-Aaa corporate spread's change in percentage points.

oil.description: Oil's return, as a fraction (0.5 is a 50% rise).

dollar.description: The broad dollar index's return, as a fraction.

volatility.description: The VIX's change in points (15 takes 20 to 35).

scenario.description: A past crisis to replay instead of shocks: dotcom_bust, bank_crisis, debt_ceiling_2011, taper_tantrum, oil_collapse, dollar_surge, q4_2018, pandemic_crash, inflation_shock, compute_bust or regional_bank_run.

years.description: Years of weekly history the betas and the factors' covariance come from. Default 5.

horizon_weeks.description: Weeks a hypothetical shock plays out over, which sets the range around the answer. Default 4.

portfolio_value.description: The portfolio's value, to give the results in money too.

annotations.title: Portfolio scenarios: macro shocks and past crises

tools.name: trade_ticks
tools.description: Every trade on Kraken's public market for a crypto pair (BTC/USD, ETH/EUR, SOL/USD) from any moment back to the market's opening, tick by tick: time to the microsecond, price, size, which side took liquidity and the order type, with the VWAP, buying against selling, the largest trades and one-minute bars built from the ticks. Up to 10,000 trades a call; next_since reads on exactly where it stopped. No key.

pair.description: A crypto pair on Kraken (BTC/USD, ETH/EUR, SOL/USD) or a coin's name (bitcoin reads BTC/USD).

start.description: The moment to read from: an ISO time (2024-01-01T14:30:00Z) or a date (its UTC midnight). A time without a zone is UTC.

since.description: Instead of start: next_since from an earlier answer, to read on exactly where it stopped (or to poll for newer trades).

requests.description: Requests of up to 1,000 trades each. Default 2.

ticks.description: Return the trades themselves (the first 1,000; the summary and bars cover all read). Default true.

tools.name: trade_flows
tools.description: What countries buy from and sell to each other, by product, from UN Comtrade: who supplies a country's chips, oil or soybeans and with what share, or how one partner's share moved year by year (in US dollars and kilograms). Products by HS code or plain words. Names Taiwan (listed as Other Asia, nes) and says how much of a total names no partner, which customs offices sometimes withhold. Goods, customs figures a year or two behind. No key.

reporter.description: The country whose customs reported the trade: a name (Germany, South Korea) or an ISO code (DEU, KR).

product.description: An HS code (2, 4 or 6 digits: 85, 8542, 271111) or plain words (semiconductors, chip-making equipment, crude oil, LNG, cars, phones, lithium-ion batteries, solar panels, rare earths, lithium carbonate, copper, iron ore, steel, soybeans, wheat, coffee, pharmaceuticals, aircraft). Default all goods.

partner.description: One partner country, to follow the trade between the two year by year with its share of the reporter's total. Leave out to rank every partner in one year.

years.description: Years to read. Default the latest five with data for one partner, or the latest with data for every partner.

limit.description: Partners to list when ranking. Default 15.

tools.name: standardized_financials
tools.description: A company's income statement, balance sheet and cash flow in one template whether it files US GAAP or IFRS, 26 lines with 14 ratios, each figure saying which tag it came from or the arithmetic that made it. One company over up to 10 fiscal years, or up to five side by side (Apple beside TSMC beside SAP), optionally in US dollars at each year's average and year-end rates. From annual reports at SEC, restatements applied.

companies.description: One company for its years, or up to five side by side (latest fiscal year each): tickers (AAPL, TSM), CIKs or names.

years.description: Fiscal years for one company. Default 5.

in_usd.description: Convert a non-dollar filer's amounts to US dollars: flows at the fiscal year's average rate, balances at its year-end rate (the local server, which reads prices). Default false.

annotations.title: Financials in one template across US GAAP and IFRS

tools.name: bond_offerings
tools.description: The bonds a company sold, tranche by tranche, from the SEC filings that priced them: amount, coupon, maturity, price, yield, spread over Treasuries (mid-swaps for euro bonds, the index for floating notes), benchmark and CUSIP from each final term sheet, with the XBRL fee tables of final prospectuses confirming amounts and adding deals priced without one. Each dollar yield is recomputed from its price. Yearly totals by currency. Registered deals only.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name. A financing arm files under its own name: pass Ford Motor Credit or Toyota Motor Credit, not the parent.

years.description: How far back to look; default 5.

deals.description: The most recent term sheets to read, newest first; default 10.

tools.name: financial_cycle
tools.description: Where countries stand in their financial cycle, from the Bank for International Settlements: house prices (real and nominal, with the change on a year), the share of income households and companies spend servicing debt, credit to households, companies and government as a share of GDP, and real and nominal effective exchange rates. Up to eight countries side by side, 40 to 60 economies covered, with history. No key.

countries.description: ISO country codes, e.g. ["CA", "AU", "CN"]; XM is the euro area.

measures.description: house_prices, debt_service, credit and exchange_rate. Default all four.

periods.description: Quarters of history for each series (months three times as many for exchange rates). Default 8.

annotations.title: House prices, debt service, credit and exchange rates by country

tools.name: treasury_cash
tools.description: The Treasury's cash at the Fed each business day since 2005 (the Treasury General Account, from the Daily Treasury Statement), its change and range over the window, and optionally the last day's largest deposits and withdrawals by category (taxes withheld, debt issued and redeemed, interest, Social Security) with month and fiscal year to date.

flows.description: Also the last day's largest deposits and withdrawals by category, with the month and fiscal year to date.

tools.name: fed_liquidity
tools.description: The Fed's footprint in the money markets: the overnight reverse repo facility's daily take-up and the standing repo facility's lending (New York Fed, its test trades kept apart), the Fed's securities holdings week by week with the pace they change by type, and its balance sheet: total assets, reserve balances, the TGA and net liquidity (assets less the TGA and the reverse repo). Each with changes over a week, four weeks and a year, a plain summary first; or any of them day by day or week by week. No key.

view.description: overview (default): the latest of each with its changes; operations: the reverse repo and standing repo facilities day by day; holdings: the Fed's securities week by week; balance_sheet: total assets, reserves, the TGA, the reverse repo and net liquidity week by week.

days.description: operations: business days shown, latest last; default 20.

weeks.description: holdings and balance_sheet: weeks shown, latest last; default 13.

annotations.title: Fed liquidity: repo facilities, holdings, reserves

tools.name: money_markets
tools.description: The US money markets' plumbing, no key: overnight repo by segment (SOFR, TGCR, BGCR, tri-party without the Fed, GCF, cleared bilateral DVP), each rate with its volume and its spread to the Fed's interest on reserves and overnight reverse repo rate; what US money market funds hold by type and whom their repo is with (Form N-MFP, via the OFR); and primary dealers' net Treasury positions by maturity (New York Fed). part gives one with its history.

part.description: One part with its history: repo (each segment's rate and volume day by day, against the Fed's rates), money_funds (what US money market funds hold, month by month) or dealers (primary dealers' net Treasury positions, week by week). Default: all three, latest.

periods.description: part: observations shown, latest last; default 20 for repo, 13 for money_funds and dealers.

annotations.title: Money markets: repo, money funds and dealers

tools.name: inflation_nowcast
tools.description: The Cleveland Fed's daily nowcast of inflation not yet published: its estimate of CPI, core CPI, PCE and core PCE for the coming months and the quarter, on the month, on a year and annualized, beside the last month published. month gives one month's nowcast day by day and its figure once out; record sets the last nowcast before each release against the published figure, with the average miss. A plain summary first. No key.

measure.description: cpi, core_cpi, pce or core_pce; default all four.

month.description: A target month (YYYY-MM): its nowcast day by day, and the published figure once out.

record.description: The nowcast's record: its last nowcast before each release against the published figure, month by month.

months.description: record: published months shown, latest last; default 12.

tools.name: rate_expectations
tools.description: What the futures market expects the Fed to do: from 30-day fed funds futures, the rate implied after each scheduled FOMC meeting, the expected change there and from today, the chances of no change, a hike or a cut, and of each target range after each meeting, by the method CME's FedWatch publishes, with the contracts behind it and today's range and effective rate. A plain summary first. No key.

meetings.description: Scheduled FOMC meetings shown, soonest first; default 8.

annotations.title: Fed rate odds from futures (FedWatch method)

tools.name: job_postings
tools.description: Labour demand as Indeed sees it, day by day: job postings against 1 February 2020 (= 100), seasonally adjusted, in the US, Canada, the UK, Australia, Germany, France, Ireland, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and the euro area, with the change over four weeks, a quarter and a year and the distance from the peak; by occupational sector or by state, province or region, ranked; or every economy side by side. Indeed Hiring Lab data (CC BY 4.0). No key.

country.description: US (default), CA, GB, AU, DE, FR, IE, IT, ES, NL or EA (the euro area), by code or name; "all" sets every one side by side.

by.description: total (default): the country's postings; sector: each occupational sector, ranked by its change on a year; region: each state, province or region.

weeks.description: total: weeks shown, a row a week, latest last; default 13.

tools.name: reserve_currencies
tools.description: What the world's central banks hold their foreign exchange reserves in, from the IMF's COFER: each currency's share of the reserves whose currency is reported (the dollar, euro, yen, sterling, renminbi and others) and its value in dollars at the latest quarter, the change in share on a year and over ten years, and the shares quarter by quarter. A plain summary first. No key.

quarters.description: Quarters of shares shown, latest last; default 8.

annotations.title: Currencies of the world's reserves (IMF COFER)

tools.name: housing_market
tools.description: The US housing market, nationally or for a metro area: Zillow's typical home value with its change on a month, a year and five years and its distance from the peak; Realtor.com's listings (median listing price, active and new listings, days on market, the share with a price cut, pending sales), each against a year earlier; and the 30-year mortgage rate. rank lists the largest metros by how fast home values rise or fall. A plain summary first. No key.

area.description: "US" (default) or a metro area by its main city ("Austin", "Austin, TX", "New York").

rank.description: Instead of one area: the largest metros ranked by the change in home values on a year.

metros.description: rank: how many of the largest metros are ranked; default 100.

limit.description: rank: metros listed; default 15.

tools.name: gdp_nowcast
tools.description: The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow, its running estimate of real GDP before the BEA publishes it (annualized): the latest nowcast and each update since the first with the data releases behind it, what each part of spending adds and each part's own pace, the BEA's latest estimates beside it, and the model's record against the BEA's advance estimates. Read from the Atlanta Fed's workbook. A plain summary first. No key.

quarters.description: Quarters of the track record shown, latest first; default 8.

tools.name: consumer_expectations
tools.description: What American households expect, from the New York Fed's Survey of Consumer Expectations, monthly: inflation over one, three and five years, home prices, the prices of gas, food, rent, medical care and college, earnings, income and spending, and the chances of losing or finding a job, of higher unemployment, of missing a debt payment and of stocks rising; the latest month beside a month and a year before, or one topic month by month. No key.

topic.description: One topic month by month, every measure the survey gives for it (medians, quartiles): inflation, home_prices, prices, earnings, income, spending, jobs, job_finding, unemployment, delinquency, interest_rates, stocks or government_debt; default the headline of each, latest month.

months.description: topic: months shown, latest last; default 13.

tools.name: margin_debt
tools.description: How much investors borrow against their stocks, from FINRA's monthly margin statistics since 1997: margin debt (customers' debit balances at member firms) with its change on a month and a year, the record and how far the latest is from it, the free credit balances in cash and margin accounts, and the months before. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: options_sentiment
tools.description: How much protection options traders buy, from Cboe's daily market statistics: the total, equity, index, ETF, VIX and SPX put/call ratios of the latest trading day with the calls and puts traded, and the total, equity, index and SPX ratios day by day with their 10- and 20-day averages. A plain summary first. No key.

days.description: Trading days shown, latest last; default 20.

tools.name: recession_watch
tools.description: The indicators read for a US recession, each beside the line it is read against and whether it is past it: the New York Fed's yield-curve model (the chance of being in recession twelve months ahead, computed as the New York Fed publishes it, month by month), the Sahm rule, the 10-year less 2-year curve and its last inversion, jobless claims against a year earlier, the Chauvet-Piger probability, GDPNow, and the Fed Board staff's excess bond premium model. A plain summary first. No key.

months.description: Months of the yield-curve model's probability shown, latest last; default 13.

tools.name: state_economy
tools.description: A US state's economy beside the nation's: the unemployment rate, payroll jobs, the Philadelphia Fed's coincident index of activity, house prices (FHFA) and real GDP, each with its change on a year; or every state and DC ranked by unemployment or by the growth of jobs, activity or house prices. A plain summary first. No key.

state.description: A state or DC by name or postal code ("Texas", "TX").

rank.description: Instead of one state: every state and DC ranked by this measure (unemployment by its rate, the others by their change on a year).

annotations.title: US state economies (BLS, FHFA, BEA, Philadelphia Fed)

tools.name: inflation_breakdown
tools.description: What is driving US consumer prices, from the BLS's CPI: all items and core beside food (at home and away), energy and gasoline, core goods and used cars, core services, shelter, rent, owners' equivalent rent, medical care and transportation services, each on the month (seasonally adjusted), over three months at an annual rate and on a year as the BLS states it, with the headline and core month by month. A plain summary first. No key.

months.description: Months of the headline and core shown, latest last; default 13.

tools.name: fed_speeches
tools.description: What the Federal Reserve Board says, from its own feeds: the latest speeches and testimony by its members and its monetary policy releases (statements, minutes), with speaker, title, date, venue and link; one member's; or one speech read, its paragraphs on monetary policy and the economy quoted as given. A plain summary first. No key.

speaker.description: A Board member by surname (Powell, Waller, Bowman...): that member's speeches and testimony.

kind.description: speech, testimony or policy (the FOMC's statements, minutes and other monetary policy releases); default all three.

limit.description: Most items listed, newest first; default 15.

read.description: A speech or testimony page on federalreserve.gov (a link from the list): its paragraphs on monetary policy, quoted.

tools.name: central_bank_speeches
tools.description: What central bankers everywhere are saying, from the BIS's collection of their speeches: the latest fifty with speaker, role and bank, title, date and link; one bank's (ECB, Bank of England, Bundesbank, Bank of Japan...) or one speaker's; or one speech read, brief excerpts of its passages on policy. A plain summary first. No key.

bank.description: A central bank by name or short name (ECB, Bank of England, Bundesbank, BoJ, RBA...): its speakers' speeches.

speaker.description: A speaker by surname (Lagarde, Bailey, Nagel...).

limit.description: Most speeches listed, newest first; default 15.

read.description: A speech page on bis.org (a link from the list): its paragraphs on monetary policy, quoted.

tools.name: financial_conditions
tools.description: How loose or tight US financial conditions are and how much stress markets show, in one answer: the OFR's daily Financial Stress Index with what credit, equity valuation, safe assets, funding and volatility each add; the Chicago Fed's NFCI and its parts; the St. Louis and Kansas City Feds' stress indexes; corporate bond spreads by rating (ICE BofA), Moody's Baa spread and the Fed Board's excess bond premium; the VIX. Each with its changes and its place in its own history.

measure.description: One measure's history instead of the overview: ofr_fsi, nfci, anfci, nfci_risk, nfci_credit, nfci_leverage, stlfsi, kcfsi, gz_spread, excess_bond_premium, investment_grade, bbb, high_yield, ccc, emerging_markets, euro_high_yield, baa_spread, vix.

periods.description: measure: observations shown, latest last; default 26.

start.description: measure: from this date instead (YYYY-MM-DD), up to 600 observations.

tools.name: market_breadth
tools.description: How many of an index's members take part in its moves, computed from the members themselves: the share of the S&P 500's (or the S&P 400's, the Dow's, or one sector's) members above their 50- and 200-day averages, how many rose and fell, new 52-week highs and lows, how far the typical member is below its high, the average member's return beside the index's own over a day, a month, the year to date and a year, recent sessions' breadth, and by_sector for the eleven sectors.

index.description: S&P 500 (default), S&P 400, Dow, or a Select Sector SPDR's ticker (XLK, XLF, XLE...) for breadth inside one sector.

by_sector.description: S&P 500: the same measures for each of its eleven sectors (reads the Select Sector SPDRs' holdings too).

days.description: Sessions of daily breadth shown, latest last; default 20.

annotations.title: Market breadth: how many members take part

tools.name: labor_market
tools.description: The US jobs picture in one answer: payroll gains with the three-month average, the unemployment rate and U-6, participation and the prime-age employment ratio, wages and hours, JOLTS openings, quits and layoffs with openings per unemployed person, and weekly jobless claims, each beside the reading before and a year before, with payroll gains month by month. A plain summary first. No key.

months.description: Months of payroll gains and the unemployment rate shown, latest last; default 13.

annotations.title: US jobs report in one answer

tools.name: commodity_prices
tools.description: World commodity prices from the World Bank's Pink Sheet, monthly since 1960: oil, gas, LNG and coal, metals and precious metals, grains, oilseeds, coffee, cocoa, sugar, cotton, rubber, timber and fertilizers, each with its change on a month, a year and five years, beside the World Bank's sector indexes; or one commodity month by month with its record; all for every commodity. A plain summary first. No key.

commodity.description: One commodity by name (copper, Brent, iron ore, cocoa, urea, LNG...): its price month by month with its record.

all.description: Every commodity in the Pink Sheet (about seventy), not only the headline ones.

months.description: commodity: months shown, latest last; default 25.

tools.name: federal_budget
tools.description: The US federal budget month by month from the Monthly Treasury Statement (since 2015): receipts, outlays and the deficit for this fiscal year and the last, and the fiscal year to date against the same months a year earlier, for the latest statement or any month's.

statement.description: The month of the Monthly Treasury Statement to read (it covers its fiscal year to that month). Default the latest.

tools.name: crypto_options
tools.description: Crypto options from Deribit's public data: each expiry's at-the-money implied volatility, call and put open interest, put/call ratio and the day's volume, with DVOL (Deribit's 30-day implied volatility index) for BTC and ETH; or one expiry's chain, strike by strike, with bids, asks and implied volatilities in US dollars. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and others.

currency.description: The coin: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB and others Deribit lists options on.

view.description: summary: every expiry's at-the-money volatility, open interest and volume, with DVOL. chain: one expiry strike by strike. Default summary.

expiry.description: For chain: the expiry date; default the nearest at least a day away.

tools.name: treasury_yields
tools.description: US Treasury daily yields from the Treasury itself: the par yield curve (1 month to 30 years), real (TIPS) yields or bill rates, for the latest day, a date, or a date range. In percent.

curve.description: nominal (par yield curve, 1 month to 30 years; default), real (TIPS), or bills.

date.description: One day (the latest on or before it). Default: the latest published.

start.description: A range instead of one day: first date.

end.description: Last date of the range; default today.

tools.name: economic_series
tools.description: Any FRED economic series (inflation, unemployment, GDP, payrolls, rates, credit spreads, oil, FX, money supply, recession indicators) by id or plain words, as dates and values, optionally as changes or year-over-year rates. as_of reads it as published on a past date (ALFRED vintages: before later revisions), and revisions shows each value then against now. Feed values straight into analysis tools.

series.description: A FRED series id (DGS10, CPIAUCSL, UNRATE) or plain words ("core inflation", "10 year treasury yield").

transform.description: level (default), change from the previous observation, pct_change (fraction), or yoy (fraction against the value a year earlier).

last.description: Only the most recent n observations.

as_of.description: The series as it was published on this date (ALFRED's vintage): only what had been released by then, at the values then shown, before later revisions.

revisions.description: With as_of: each date's value then against today's, and how much it was revised.

tools.name: price_history
tools.description: Price bars (open, high, low, close, volume), monthly to one-minute, for US stocks and ETFs, stocks listed abroad (SAP.DE, 7203.T), currency pairs (EUR/USD), futures (crude oil, gold), indices and yields (S&P 500, VIX, 10 year yield) and crypto (bitcoin), by symbol or plain name. Stocks adjust for splits and dividends by default (adjustment: none is as traded), with dividends, splits and the total return; returns: true adds daily returns. No key needed; uses the user's Alpaca or Tiingo key for US stocks when set.

symbol.description: A ticker (AAPL, BRK.B), a stock listed abroad with its market suffix (SAP.DE, 7203.T, SHEL.L, 0700.HK), a currency pair (EUR/USD), a future (CL=F, or "crude oil", "gold"), an index (^GSPC, or "S&P 500", "VIX", "10 year yield") or a crypto pair (BTC/USD, or "bitcoin").

start.description: First date; default one year ago.

interval.description: Bar size; default 1Day. Minute bars go back 30 days at 1Min and 60 days at 5 to 30 minutes on the keyless source (default: the last 5 days); Tiingo is daily only.

adjusted.description: Split- and dividend-adjusted; default true. false is adjustment: none, prices as traded.

adjustment.description: all: adjusted for splits and dividends (the default); splits: for splits only, so prices compare across a split and leave dividends out; none: as traded each day, the price a trade or a filing of that date shows.

returns.description: Also return simple returns from close to close (returns[i] is from dates[i] to dates[i+1]), ready for beta, correlation or Sharpe tools.

tools.name: fund_portfolio
tools.description: What a US mutual fund or ETF holds, from its own SEC Form N-PORT (VOO, IVV, QQQ, AGG, FXAIX): every position with value and weight, exposure by asset type, issuer, country and currency, a bond fund's coupon and maturity profile, its monthly returns, the money that came in and went out each month, and what changed since the previous quarter.

fund.description: A mutual fund or ETF ticker (VOO, IVV, QQQ, AGG, FXAIX, ARKK) or an SEC series id (S000004310).

period.description: Report date, the last day of a fiscal quarter's last month (2026-06-30); default the latest public one.

top.description: Most positions to list, by value; default 25.

compare.description: Also compare with the previous public report; default true.

tools.name: options_chain
tools.description: An option chain from Cboe's delayed data for a stock, ETF or index (AAPL, SPY, SPX, VIX): bids, asks, implied volatility, greeks, open interest and volume by strike for one expiration, every expiration with its open interest, put/call ratios, max pain and the move the at-the-money straddle prices in.

symbol.description: A stock or ETF (AAPL, SPY, QQQ) or an index (SPX, NDX, RUT, VIX, XSP).

expiration.description: An expiration date (2026-11-20), or "nearest" (default); the result lists every expiration.

window.description: Strikes within this fraction of the underlying price; default 0.1 (10 percent).

min_open_interest.description: Only contracts with at least this open interest; default 0.

tools.name: volatility_surface
tools.description: The implied volatility surface from Cboe's delayed option data: at-the-money IV by expiration (term structure), 25-delta put and call IV with the risk reversal and butterfly (skew), and IV at fixed moneyness from 80 to 120 percent of the price (smile).

symbol.description: A stock or ETF (AAPL, SPY) or an index (SPX, NDX, RUT, VIX).

expirations.description: How many expirations from the nearest; default 8.

tools.name: futures_curve
tools.description: A Cboe futures curve from its daily settlements: VIX futures by expiration with the VIX index, contango or backwardation and the front month's premium; also mini VIX, variance, bitcoin and iBoxx bond index futures.

product.description: A Cboe futures product: VIX (default), mini VIX, S&P 500 variance, bitcoin, or the iBoxx high yield, investment grade and emerging market bond index futures.

tools.name: figure_trace
tools.description: How a reported figure is built, from the filing itself: the lines the company's own XBRL calculation adds up to it, each line's value, every sum recomputed and checked, what the figure feeds into, and how the filing splits it by segment, product or region. It shows the filing agrees with itself, not that the figures are right.

measure.description: revenue, net_income, operating_income, gross_profit, cost_of_revenue, operating_expenses, pretax_income, total_assets, current_assets, total_liabilities, current_liabilities, equity, operating_cash_flow, or any tag the filing uses (NetCashProvidedByUsedInInvestingActivities, or us-gaap:Assets).

year.description: The calendar year the report's period ends in. Default the latest filed.

tools.name: filing_check
tools.description: Every number in a 10-K or 10-Q read twice: as a person reads the document and as machines read its inline XBRL. Lists each figure tagged at a scale other than the unit its table or words state, each fact tagged twice with different values, each sum in the filing's own calculation that does not add up, and each fact SEC's company facts hold differently or not at all, with a link to the figure, and counts of what was checked.

accession.description: Check this filing (a 10-K or 10-Q, or an amendment of one), whatever form says.

filings.description: Check the latest this many filings of the form, newest first; default 1.

annotations.title: Filing check: the document against its XBRL

tools.name: source_check
tools.description: Whether the documents behind an answer are still the bytes it was read from: give the evidence rows (or a canli-mcp receipt's sources) and each document is read again, past every cache, as the same, changed since, or unreachable. Only documents from the sources this server reads are fetched.

url.description: The document's address, as the evidence or the receipt gives it.

sources.description: The documents to check: evidence rows, or a receipt's sources.

annotations.title: Source check: are the documents still the same

tools.name: token_check
tools.description: What an ERC-20 token's contract can do and how much of it exists, read from the chain: mint, pause, blacklist and upgrade powers, owner, proxy, source verification, supply, and an unlock schedule you give set against it. It names what the code allows. A clean reading never means safe, and it cannot detect a rug pull.

announced_max_supply.description: The maximum supply the project states, in whole tokens.

schedule.description: The unlock schedule the project announces, in whole tokens. The chain does not state one, so it comes from you.

tools.name: segment_revenue
tools.description: Where a company's revenue comes from, read from the XBRL of its latest 10-K (or 10-Q): revenue and operating income by business segment, revenue by product or service and by region, for up to three years, with the company's own labels and each breakdown checked against total revenue.

form.description: Annual (10-K, default: fiscal years) or quarterly (10-Q: the quarter).

tools.name: index_constituents
tools.description: The members of a stock index (S&P 500, S&P 400, the Dow, Nasdaq 100, Russell 2000, MSCI EAFE, a Select Sector) with their weights: from the latest day's holdings State Street publishes (SPY, MDY, DIA, the sector SPDRs), or the N-PORT of an ETF that tracks the index, with the date, the number of members and how concentrated the top ten are. as_of gives the members on a past date from the ETF's N-PORT for that quarter, companies since removed included; changes_from lists who joined and who left between two dates.

index.description: An index by name ("S&P 500", "Nasdaq 100", "Russell 2000", "S&P 400", "MSCI EAFE", "Dow Jones"), or the ticker of an ETF that tracks the index you want (VOO, IWM, XLK).

source.description: daily (default where State Street publishes the fund's holdings each day: the S&P 500 through SPY, the S&P 400 through MDY, the Dow through DIA, the Select Sector SPDRs) or nport (the latest N-PORT, a quarter old).

limit.description: Most members to list, by weight; default 50.

as_of.description: A past date: the members as the tracking ETF's N-PORT reported them for the last quarter-end on or before it, companies since removed included, so a backtest's universe has no survivorship bias.

changes_from.description: An earlier date: also list the members added and removed between the report for it and the one used (as_of, or the latest).

tools.name: fomc
tools.description: The Federal Reserve's rate decisions from its own record: each FOMC meeting of a year (held and scheduled), the action, change and target range, the vote with dissenters and their reasons, links to statements and minutes, the latest statement, and the median projections (dot plot) for GDP, unemployment, inflation and the federal funds rate.

year.description: Meetings and decisions of this year; default this year.

tools.name: economic_calendar
tools.description: The US economic calendar from the agencies' own schedules: when BLS (jobs, CPI, PPI, JOLTS), BEA (GDP, personal income and PCE, trade), the Census Bureau (retail sales, housing starts, durable goods) and the Fed (FOMC decisions) release, with times in US Eastern and the market-moving releases flagged.

until.description: Last date; default 30 days after since.

key_only.description: Only the releases markets watch most (jobs, CPI, PPI, JOLTS, GDP, PCE, retail sales, housing starts, durable goods, trade, the employment cost index, FOMC decisions).

tools.name: executive_pay
tools.description: What a company's executives are paid against how it did, from the pay-versus-performance table in its proxy: the CEO's reported pay and the pay actually earned, the other executives' averages, shareholder return against peers, net income and the company's chosen measure, five years; or every company's CEO pay ranked, with mis-scaled filings held out.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name. Without it, every company that tagged a pay-versus-performance table for the year, ranked.

year.description: Across the market, the fiscal year (by calendar year); default last year.

rank_by.description: Across the market: the CEO's reported pay (default), pay actually paid, or total shareholder return.

limit.description: Across the market, most companies to list; default 25.

tools.name: short_interest
tools.description: Short interest in US stocks from FINRA, twice a month: shares short, the change, average daily volume and days to cover over several reports, and the share of shares outstanding from the company's latest SEC cover page; or, with no stock, the market ranked by days to cover, change or size.

symbol.description: A US stock ticker. Without it, the whole market at the latest settlement date, ranked.

periods.description: Settlement dates to show for a stock, newest last; default 6 (three months).

rank_by.description: Across the market: days to cover (default), the change since the last report, or shares short.

min_volume.description: Across the market, only stocks averaging at least this many shares a day; default 1,000,000, so thin stocks do not crowd the list.

limit.description: Across the market, most stocks to list; default 25.

tools.name: portfolio_rules
tools.description: Where your holdings stand against the US lines that bring a filing or cap concentration: more than 5% of a company's class (Schedule 13D or 13G), more than 10% (Section 16 insider), $100 million in 13(f) securities (Form 13F), and the 75-5-10 and RIC diversification tests; each position's share of its class from the last cover page and days to exit from FINRA's volume. A check, not compliance advice.

symbol.description: A US-listed ticker (AAPL, BRK.B) or a CIK.

shares.description: Shares held (depositary shares for an ADR).

value.description: Market value in US dollars. Without it or price, the latest price is read where this server has prices.

price.description: Price per share in US dollars, when value is not given.

fund.description: true for an ETF or other investment company: the diversification tests count it as qualifying at any size.

cash.description: Cash, receivables and US Government securities in US dollars: part of total assets, and qualifying in the diversification tests.

participation.description: The share of a day's volume you would sell into, for days to exit; default 0.2.

tools.name: off_exchange_volume
tools.description: How much of a US stock trades away from the exchanges, from FINRA's OTC transparency data: weekly shares and trades in dark pools (ATSs) and with other off-exchange dealers, and the largest dark pools and dealers in the latest week.

weeks.description: Weeks to show, newest last; default 8. FINRA publishes Tier 1 stocks two weeks after the week, others four.

tools.name: fails_to_deliver
tools.description: Shares that failed to settle, from the SEC's fails-to-deliver data (NSCC): a stock's outstanding fail balance on each settlement date over the latest half-month files, with prices and dollar values, or the securities with the largest fails across the market.

symbol.description: A ticker. Without it, the securities with the largest fails by value in the latest file.

files.description: Half-month files to read, newest first; default 2 (about a month) for a ticker, 1 across the market.

limit.description: Across the market, most securities to list; default 25.

tools.name: futures_positioning
tools.description: Who holds what in a futures market, from the CFTC's weekly Commitments of Traders: long, short and net positions of producers, swap dealers, managed money and others (or dealers, asset managers and leveraged funds for financial futures), with weekly changes and where the speculators sit in their range, by market name (gold, crude oil, 10 year note, euro, bitcoin).

market.description: A futures market by name ("gold", "crude oil", "corn", "s&p 500", "10 year note", "euro", "bitcoin", "vix") or a CFTC contract market code (088691).

weeks.description: Weekly reports to return, newest last; default 52.

tools.name: private_offerings
tools.description: Private markets from Form D, filed when startups and funds sell securities without registering: amount offered and sold, number of investors, minimum investment, exemption (Rule 506(b) or 506(c)), industry, fund type and the people behind it, for one issuer or across the market (newest first, filtered by industry or amount sold).

company.description: An issuer by name or CIK (a startup, a fund). Without it, the latest Form D filings across the market.

industry.description: Across the market, keep issuers whose Form D industry group contains these words: "Pooled Investment Fund", "Biotechnology", "Other Technology", "Real Estate", "Banking".

min_sold.description: Across the market, keep offerings that have sold at least this many dollars.

since.description: Filed on or after this date; default seven days ago across the market, ten years for an issuer.

limit.description: Most offerings to list; default 20. Across the market at most 100 filings are read to find them.

tools.name: company_events
tools.description: Company news from the source: the events companies must report on Form 8-K (earnings, deals, executive changes, restatements, auditor changes, bankruptcies, cyber incidents, layoffs, delisting notices), for one company or, by event, across the whole market, each with the headline of the press release it attached and the opening of what the filing says.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name. Without it, filings across the whole market (then event is required).

event.description: Which events: an item number (2.02) or a name: earnings, material_agreement, acquisition_or_sale_completed, executive_change, restatement, auditor_change, bankruptcy, cybersecurity_incident, restructuring, impairment, delisting_notice, new_debt, shareholder_vote, regulation_fd, other_event. Default: all, for a company.

since.description: Filed on or after this date; default 180 days ago for a company, 30 days across the market.

until.description: Filed on or before this date; default today.

limit.description: Most events to list; default 15.

excerpts.description: Read each filing for the opening of what it says and its press release's headline; default true (up to three requests per filing).

tools.name: latest_filings
tools.description: What has just been filed with the SEC, across every company: EDGAR's latest-filings feed, newest first by acceptance time, filtered by form (8-K, 10-K, 4, SC 13D, S-1...), 8-K event (earnings, executive change, restatement, bankruptcy), words in the filer's name and time. For watching what comes in today and over the last few business days; list_filings and company_events reach further back.

forms.description: Form types, e.g. ["8-K"], ["10-K", "10-Q"], ["4"], ["SC 13D"], ["S-1"]; each also matches its amendments (8-K/A). Default: every form.

event.description: 8-K filings with this item only: an item number (2.02) or a name (earnings, executive_change, restatement, bankruptcy, cybersecurity_incident...).

company.description: Words that must all appear in the filer's name, e.g. "bancorp" or "apple".

since.description: Accepted at or after this time (a date means its start, US Eastern). Default: everything the feed holds.

limit.description: Most filings to list; default 40.

tools.name: filing_diff
tools.description: What changed in a company's 10-K (or 10-Q) against the one before, section by section (risk factors by default, MD&A, business, legal proceedings): new and dropped paragraphs, the sentences changed in the rest, and the words whose use rose or fell most.

section.description: The item to compare: "risk factors" (default), "md&a", "business", "legal proceedings", "market risk", "1A"...

form.description: Default 10-K: the latest annual report against the one before.

accession.description: The newer filing; default the latest.

against.description: The older filing; default the one filed before the newer.

threshold.description: Word-pair overlap at which two paragraphs are the same paragraph. Default 0.5.

max_items.description: Most new, dropped and changed paragraphs listed each. Default 8; raise it to read more.

tools.name: news
tools.description: News about a company or a topic from the world's press (the GDELT Project's open index, no key): articles newest first with outlet and country, and the daily average tone of the coverage.
