query.description: Words or a "quoted phrase" to find, e.g. "\"rate cut\" Fed". With company, they narrow its news.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name: its news, searched by the company's name.

start.description: Instead of days: the first day (GDELT's search covers about the last three months).

end.description: With start: the last day (default start).

limit.description: Most articles; default 25.

language.description: Source language, e.g. english (default) or any; others by name (german, japanese...).

tone.description: Add the daily average tone of the coverage (one more request, about five seconds). Default true.

tools.name: explain_move
tools.description: Why a stock moved on a day, in one call: its return against the market and how rare it was for this stock (a market model fitted on the year before, with a z-score), the company's SEC filings around the day (8-K items named), and the press's headlines from those days.

date.description: The trading day of the move (YYYY-MM-DD).

benchmark.description: The market to compare with; default SPY.

window_days.description: Calendar days either side of the date for filings and news; default 2.

news.description: Add the press's headlines (GDELT, about five seconds). Default true.

tools.name: portfolio_xray
tools.description: A portfolio seen through its funds: each ETF or mutual fund opened into the positions of its latest SEC N-PORT and added to the stocks held directly, giving the real exposure to each company, the overlap between funds and the effective number of positions.

symbol.description: A stock (AAPL) or a fund or ETF (VOO, QQQ, AGG, FXAIX).

weight.description: Its weight or its value: weights are rescaled to sum to 1.

top.description: Most look-through positions to list; default 25.

tools.name: comps
tools.description: A comparable-companies table: the company beside its NYSE- and Nasdaq-listed peers in the same SEC industry code, the nearest in revenue, on revenue, growth, margins, ROE, R&D intensity and FCF margin (or measures you pick), with the peers' median and the company's rank on each.

metrics.description: Measures to compare; default revenue, growth, margins, ROE, R&D intensity and FCF margin.

companies.description: The peers to compare, by ticker, CIK or name, instead of the industry's nearest in size. Foreign filers work: IFRS accounts are read and figures put in dollars.

peers.description: Peers to show, nearest in revenue; default 8.

period.description: FY2025: each company's fiscal year that best overlaps calendar 2025 (the default is the last complete year).

fiscal_year_end.description: Instead of period: each company's fiscal year ending in this window (slower: more data to read).

tools.name: debt_profile
tools.description: A company's debt from its annual reports' XBRL: total and net debt, the maturity ladder from the debt note (next 12 months to after five years), lease payments, interest expense, the implied interest rate, interest coverage and debt to EBITDA, with five years of debt and cash.

years.description: Annual history of total debt and cash to show; default 5.

tools.name: ownership_breadth
tools.description: How many institutions hold a stock, quarter by quarter: 13F filers whose holdings tables list its CUSIP (EDGAR full-text search), with the change and a sample of holders. A fall in breadth predicted lower returns (Chen, Hong and Stein 2002).

cusip.description: Or the share class's 9-character CUSIP (037833100 for Apple).

quarters.description: Quarters of 13F filings to count, newest first; default 6.

holders.description: Filers to list from the latest quarter; default 20.

tools.name: forensic_scores
tools.description: Three accounting screens in one call from the company's own annual XBRL for its last two years: Beneish's M-score (earnings manipulation), Piotroski's F-score (financial strength) and Altman's Z-score (distress), every input with its tag.

tools.name: funding_rates
tools.description: Crypto perpetual funding on OKX's USDT perpetuals, no key: each coin's latest eight-hour rate, the window's mean and its annualized carry (short the perpetual against long spot), the last week's, and the share of positive periods.

coins.description: Coin symbols, e.g. ["BTC", "ETH", "SOL"]; default BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE.

days.description: Window, in days back from now; default 30.

series.description: Also return each coin's funding by period; default false.

tools.name: compute_prices
tools.description: Compute as a market, no key: the on-demand hourly price of each data-centre GPU (B200, H200, H100, A100, L40S...) across the clouds and GPU marketplaces, the cheapest, median and dearest offer with who offers it, every provider's offer for one model, recent list-price changes, and the Cirrun GPU Index (a daily chained index of those prices). Each price is the provider's own list price with the date it was confirmed.

gpu.description: A GPU model (H100, H200, B200, A100, L40S, RTX 4090...): every provider's offer for it. Default: one row per model.

provider.description: Only this provider's offers, e.g. RunPod or AWS.

changes.description: Latest list-price changes to return; default 20.

tools.name: shareholder_returns
tools.description: What a company has paid its shareholders, year by year from its annual XBRL: dividends per share (split-adjusted record: years raised in a row, 5- and 10-year growth) and in total, buybacks and shares issued for cash, the diluted share count and its change, the payout ratio and the share of free cash flow paid out, and at the last close the dividend yield and shareholder yield.

years.description: Fiscal years to show, newest first; default 10.

price.description: Add the dividend and shareholder yields at the last close; default true.

tools.name: buybacks
tools.description: A company's share buybacks period by period from its own XBRL (SEC company facts): for each fiscal year or quarter, the cash paid for repurchases, the shares bought and the value recorded for them, the average price, the program's authorized and remaining amounts where tagged, and the change in shares outstanding. Each figure names the filing it came from (accession, form, date); a figure the company does not tag is said to be untagged, not estimated.

quarterly.description: Fiscal quarters instead of fiscal years; default false.

periods.description: Periods to show, newest first; default 10 years or 8 quarters.

tools.name: market_overview
tools.description: The market at a glance, no key: the S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow, Russell 2000 and VIX, the eleven S&P sectors (SPDR funds) ranked by the month, Treasury yields from 13 weeks to 30 years, the dollar and major currencies, oil, gas, gold, silver and copper, bitcoin and ether, and the main markets in Europe and Asia, each with its last close and its change over a day, a week, a month, three months, the year to date and a year.

groups.description: Which groups to show (us, sectors, rates, currencies, commodities, crypto, world); default all.

tools.name: federal_contracts
tools.description: What the US government obligated to a company in a fiscal year, no key: the total, by agency and industry code, its recipient entities, and its largest contracts with links, from USAspending.gov.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name; its SEC name is searched ("LOCKHEED MARTIN").

recipients.description: Or recipient names to search instead, e.g. a subsidiary ["Sikorsky"].

fiscal_year.description: US federal fiscal year (October to September); default the last complete one.

limit.description: Largest contracts to list; default 10.

tools.name: drug_pipeline
tools.description: A drug company's pipeline, no key: active clinical trials by phase, the readouts (primary completions) due in the coming months, late-stage trials, and its FDA approvals, from ClinicalTrials.gov and Drugs@FDA.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name; its SEC name is searched.

sponsor.description: Or the sponsor name as trials list it, e.g. "Vertex Pharmaceuticals".

months.description: Readouts: primary completions due within this many months; default 12.

tools.name: comment_letters
tools.description: What the SEC's staff questioned in a company's filings and how it answered: comment letters (UPLOAD) and replies (CORRESP) grouped into reviews, with the topics of the newest (non-GAAP, revenue recognition, segments...) and excerpts.

read.description: Newest letters filed as text to read for their topics and an excerpt; default 4 (PDF letters are listed, not read).

tools.name: reverse_dcf
tools.description: The free-cash-flow growth a share price implies: solves a discounted cash flow model for the growth that reaches the market's enterprise value, from the company's annual XBRL and the last close, with a sensitivity table and the company's own history beside it.

ticker.description: The ticker to price, when company is a CIK without one (a predecessor filer).

discount_rate.description: Yearly discount rate (cost of capital); default 0.09.

terminal_growth.description: Growth for ever after the forecast years; default 0.025.

years.description: Forecast years of the implied growth; default 10.

base.description: Base free cash flow: the latest year (default) or the last three years' average, which smooths an unusual year.

tools.name: bank_financials
tools.description: A US bank's condition quarter by quarter from its call reports (FDIC, no key): assets, deposits and the share uninsured, loans and the share noncurrent, equity, earnings, ROA, ROE, net interest margin and capital ratios. With no bank, failures since 1934 and their cost, by year or state.

company.description: A bank or its holding company: ticker, CIK or name (WAL, "Zions").

cert.description: Or the bank's FDIC certificate number.

quarters.description: Quarters to return, newest first; default 8.

failures.description: With no bank: the latest failures to list; default 10.

failures_year.description: With no bank: failures in one year.

failures_state.description: With no bank: failures in one state, e.g. KS.

tools.name: filing_drift
tools.description: How a 10-K section's language drifts over several years: each year's change from the year before (the Lazy Prices measure), hedging and adverse words, readability, and how much it says about a theme you name and how that wording moves, with flags for the years and themes that moved most.

section.description: The 10-K item to follow: "risk factors" (default), "md&a", "business", "market risk"...

years.description: Annual reports to compare, newest first; default 5.

theme.description: A phrase to follow through the years, e.g. "supply chain", "tariff", "China".

tools.name: planned_insider_sales
tools.description: Insiders' planned sales from Form 144, filed before they sell: seller, role, shares, market value, share of the company, approximate sale date, how the shares were acquired and any 10b5-1 plan date, with totals by seller.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name of the issuer.

days.description: Notices filed in the last this many days; default 180.

limit.description: Most notices to read, newest first; default 25.

tools.name: ipo_pipeline
tools.description: The IPO pipeline from EDGAR: companies that filed or amended a registration (S-1, F-1) in a window, labelled IPO candidate, SPAC, fund or already listed, and offerings priced (424B4) with price, shares and proceeds from the prospectus cover.

days.description: Filings in the last this many days; default 30.

kind.description: ipo (default): companies with no ticker yet; spac: blank-check companies; fund: ETF and trust registrations (crypto ETFs, say); all: every S-1 and F-1, follow-ons and resales too.

priced.description: Priced offerings (424B4) to read the cover of; default 15.

tools.name: lockup_calendar
tools.description: When insiders' shares from recent IPOs may be sold, from each company's final prospectus (424B4). Across the market, the lock-ups ending in a window: company, IPO date, length as stated (usually 180 days), the date it counts from and the expiry computed from it, staged releases, early-release triggers (earnings release, share price), shares locked up and shares sold. For one company, its terms quoted and later filings that waive or release them.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name: its IPO's lock-up terms quoted from the final prospectus, and later filings that waive or release them. Without it, the IPO lock-ups across the market that end in the window.

days.description: Across the market, the window's length in days from today (or from since); default 60.

since.description: Across the market, the window's first day (YYYY-MM-DD), for a past or later window; default today.

limit.description: Across the market, most lock-ups listed, earliest first; default 25.

tools.name: large_holders
tools.description: Who owns more than 5 percent of a company, from Schedules 13D and 13G: each holder's latest stake (shares, percent of class, voting power), whether it is passive (13G) or may seek to influence control (13D, with its stated purpose); or, with no company, the newest 13D stakes across the whole market.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name. Without it, the latest filings across the whole market (new activist stakes by default).

schedule.description: 13D (may seek to influence control; states its purpose), 13G (passive) or both. Default: both for a company, 13D across the market.

since.description: Filed on or after this date; default three years ago for a company, seven days ago across the market.

limit.description: Most filings to read; default 25.

tools.name: earnings_calendar
tools.description: Earnings dates from the companies' own 8-Ks (Item 2.02, results of operations). For a company: its recent results releases with the quarter each covered and whether it came before the open or after the close (EDGAR's acceptance time), and the next release estimated from the same quarter a year earlier, with a window. Across the market: who is due to report in a window, from when they reported in the same weeks last year, marked once they have. Estimates, not announcements.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name: its results releases and the next one estimated. Leave out for the market.

quarters.description: Past releases to list for a company; default 8.

since.description: Across the market: first day of the window; default today.

until.description: Across the market: last day; default 14 days after since, at most 31.

limit.description: Across the market: most companies to list (the largest first); default 100.

tools.name: earnings_move

instructions: Market data and research from the public sources themselves. Before answering with a company's reported figures, check them with verify_claims: each comes back confirmed, contradicted (with the filed figure and what the wrong one matches) or not reported. Across the market: screen_companies ranks every US-listed company on fundamentals, company_report gives one company's financials, segment_revenue its revenue by segment, product and region, valuation, risk, insiders and filings in one call, event_study measures price reactions to earnings or insider trades, mentions_trend counts a phrase in filings over time. Analyst work: financial_statements gives the income statement, balance sheet and cash flows exactly as filed (several years joined, restatements and splits shown, never mixed); filing_tables finds the table that holds a figure in a filing, or follows it through several years of filings (members, stores, ARPU, guidance tables); earnings_release reads a results press release: results, guidance as ranges, and last quarter's guidance against this quarter's results; release_check sets every figure in a results release against the 10-Q or 10-K filed after it and lists what changed; filing_check reads a 10-K or 10-Q twice, as a person sees it and as its inline XBRL tags it, and lists where the two disagree (a figure tagged at another scale than its table states, a fact tagged twice with different values, a sum that does not add up, a fact SEC's company facts hold differently). Companies: company_profile, list_filings, then read_filing (section "risk factors", "md&a" and so on for a 10-K or 10-Q; document "EX-99.1" for an 8-K press release); search_filings finds words across all filings; executive_pay reads a proxy's pay-versus-performance table; company_events gives a company's 8-K news (or, by event, the whole market's: restatements, bankruptcies, cyber incidents); latest_filings is what has just been filed, across every company, by form and event; filing_diff shows what changed in a 10-K's risk factors (or any item) since the last one; filing_drift follows a section over several years (how much its wording moved, hedging, readability, and a theme such as "supply chain"), flagging the years and themes that moved most; news gives the world's press coverage of a company or topic, with its tone; explain_move puts a day's move beside the filings and headlines around it; portfolio_xray opens a portfolio's funds into the companies they hold; comps sets a company beside its industry peers; debt_profile gives its debt, when it falls due and what it costs; ownership_breadth counts the institutions holding it, quarter by quarter; forensic_scores runs the Beneish, Piotroski and Altman screens on its filings; reverse_dcf solves for the growth its share price implies; shareholder_returns what it has paid its owners each year (dividends, buybacks, the share count, payout ratios, its dividend record and yields); buybacks its share repurchases by fiscal year or quarter (cash paid, shares bought, the average price, the program authorized and remaining where tagged, the share count's change), each figure with its filing; comment_letters gives what the SEC questioned in its filings and how it answered; audit_signals its going-concern doubts, auditor changes and critical audit matters, or across the market the companies that newly raised a going-concern doubt or changed auditor; federal_contracts what the US government paid it (USAspending); drug_pipeline a drug company's active trials by phase, its next readouts and its FDA approvals; bank_financials a US bank's quarterly call-report condition (uninsured deposits, bad loans, capital ratios) or the latest bank failures (FDIC). earnings_calendar gives a company's results dates and the next one estimated, or who reports in a window; earnings_move the move options price for its next results beside its shares' past reactions; earnings_season how the S&P 500's reporting season is going (how many reported, the share that beat the consensus, the median surprise, by sector, who is due). Ownership: insider_trades (Form 4), planned_insider_sales (Form 144, filed before an insider sells) and fund_holdings (a manager's 13F); large_holders (13D/13G: 5 percent holders and activists), investment_advisers (Form ADV); funds: fund_portfolio (what a mutual fund or ETF holds, its flows and returns, from N-PORT); private markets: private_offerings (Form D raises by startups and funds), ipo_pipeline (S-1/F-1 registrations and priced IPOs) and lockup_calendar (when IPO lock-ups end, read from each final prospectus); positioning: short_interest, margin_debt (FINRA's monthly margin statistics), options_sentiment (Cboe's daily market-wide put/call ratios), off_exchange_volume (FINRA dark pools), fails_to_deliver (SEC) and futures_positioning (CFTC Commitments of Traders). Rates and the economy: economic_calendar (when the data comes out), fomc (the Fed's decisions, votes and projections), fed_speeches (what Board members said lately, a speech's passages on policy), central_bank_speeches (central bankers' speeches everywhere, from the BIS), rate_expectations (what fed funds futures price for each coming FOMC meeting: the odds of a hike, hold or cut and of each target range, by FedWatch's method), fed_liquidity (the reverse repo and standing repo facilities day by day, the Fed's securities and their runoff, reserves, the TGA and net liquidity), money_markets (overnight repo by segment against the Fed's rates, what money market funds hold and whom they lend to, primary dealers' Treasury positions), treasury_yields, treasury_auctions, federal_debt, treasury_holders (who holds Treasuries, by country, from the TIC system), economic_series (FRED), inflation_nowcast (the Cleveland Fed's nowcast of CPI and PCE inflation for the months not yet published, and its record), inflation_breakdown (CPI by component: shelter, core goods and services, energy, food and more), gdp_nowcast (the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow for this quarter: each update, what each part of spending adds, its record), recession_watch (the yield-curve model, the Sahm rule, the curve, claims and more, each against its line), financial_conditions (how tight financial conditions are and how much stress markets show: the OFR's stress index, the NFCI, credit spreads by rating, the excess bond premium and the VIX, each against its own history), state_economy (a US state beside the nation, or every state ranked), consumer_expectations (the New York Fed's survey of what households expect: inflation, prices, earnings, jobs, stocks), world_series (a country's inflation, unemployment, GDP growth, policy rate, 10-year yield or exchange rate from its own statistics office or central bank, up to 30 countries side by side, any series by its publisher's code, and check: true to compare a second official publisher), world_economy (World Bank, every country), labor_market (the US jobs report in one answer: payrolls, unemployment, wages, JOLTS, claims), job_postings (Indeed's daily job postings index in eleven economies, by sector and region), reserve_currencies (the IMF's COFER: each currency's share of the world's foreign exchange reserves), housing_market (US home values from Zillow and listings from Realtor.com, nationally or by metro, with the mortgage rate) and economic_outlook (OECD projections). Beyond the US: european_filings (a company's ESEF annual report, the figures it tagged), reference_rates (SOFR, EFFR, €STR, ECB and Bank of England rates from the central banks, and about forty central banks' policy rates), prediction_markets (Polymarket and Kalshi prices for an outcome) and crypto_fundamentals (DefiLlama: a protocol's value locked, fees and revenue, a chain's value locked, a stablecoin's supply) and funding_rates (perpetual funding and its annualized carry, OKX). Commodities: commodity_prices (the World Bank's Pink Sheet: oil, gas, metals, grains, fertilizers and more, monthly since 1960), crop_outlook (the USDA's WASDE balance sheets for grains, oilseeds and cotton by country, and this month's revisions) and energy_report (the EIA's weekly US oil and gas report: crude, Cushing, gasoline and distillate stocks against the five-year average, refinery utilization, production, trade and demand, and natural gas in storage). Compute: compute_prices (what an hour of each data-centre GPU costs on demand across the clouds, and the Cirrun GPU Index). Options: options_chain, volatility_surface and futures_curve (Cboe delayed data). The market at a glance: market_overview (US indices and the VIX, the eleven sectors ranked by the month, Treasury yields, the dollar, oil, gold, bitcoin and markets abroad, each over a day, a week, a month, three months, the year to date and a year) and market_breadth (how many S&P 500, S&P 400, Dow or sector members are above their 50- and 200-day averages, rising, at 52-week highs or lows, and the average member against the index, by sector). Prices: price_history for stocks in the US and abroad, currencies, futures, indices and crypto (no key needed; the user's Alpaca or Tiingo key is used for US stocks when set). Every result has its source URL; cite it.
